title: Eight weeks into one Jewish learning journey
audience: Independent adult beginners who can decode Hebrew phonetically and need guided English support.
principle: Gemara is the reading-and-reasoning spine; each wider-canon encounter supplies a source form, question, or practice that makes the spine more intelligible.

weeks.practice: Identify a source's voice, setting, and first question.
Distinguish a textual claim from the act of prayer it later informs.
Name a category, its limit, and the boundary between studying a rule and applying it.
Map competing claims and explain one ethical tension without flattening it.
Ask what purpose a stated measure or claim serves before judging it.
Connect a textual boundary to a community and historical setting.
Compare two sources: name a genuine difference and one responsible point of connection.
Read an unfamiliar source, state one uncertainty, and choose the next targeted repair.

completionRule: Every week ends with retrieval or unfamiliar-source transfer; completion routes back to the Gemara spine with only a meaningful optional lateral connection.
